segs.e: Linked Discourses 6.1
1. The Appeal
The Appeal of the Divinity
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

segs.p: “adhigato kho myāyaṁ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo.
segs.e: “This principle I have discovered is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, comprehensible to the astute.

segs.p: Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṁ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā.
segs.e: But people like clinging, they love it and enjoy it.

segs.p: Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya duddasaṁ idaṁ ṭhānaṁ yadidaṁ idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppādo.
segs.e: It’s hard for them to see this topic; that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination.

segs.p: Idampi kho ṭhānaṁ duddasaṁ yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s also hard for them to see this topic; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṁ deseyyaṁ; pare ca me na ājāneyyuṁ; so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā”ti.
segs.e: And if I were to teach this principle, others might not understand me, which would be wearying and troublesome for me.”

segs.p: Apissu bhagavantaṁ imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṁsu pubbe assutapubbā:
segs.e: And then these verses, which were neither supernaturally inspired, nor learned before in the past, occurred to the Buddha:
“I’ve struggled hard to realize this,
there’s no need to reveal it now!
Those mired in greed and hate
can’t really understand this teaching.
It goes against the stream, subtle,
deep, obscure, and very fine.
Those besotted by greed cannot see,
for they’re cloaked in a mass of darkness.”

segs.p: Itiha bhagavato paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṁ namati, no dhammadesanāya.
segs.e: And as the Buddha reflected like this, his mind inclined to remaining passive, not to teaching the Dhamma.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmuno sahampatissa bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya etadahosi:
segs.e: Then, knowing the Buddha’s train of thought, it occurred to the divinity Sahampati,

segs.p: “nassati vata bho loko, vinassati vata bho loko, yatra hi nāma tathāgatassa arahato sammāsambuddhassa appossukkatāya cittaṁ namati, no dhammadesanāyā”ti.
segs.e: “Oh lord! The world will be lost, the world will perish! For the mind of the Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, inclines to remaining passive, not to teaching the Dhamma.”

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā dakkhiṇajāṇumaṇḍalaṁ pathaviyaṁ nihantvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He arranged his robe over one shoulder, knelt on his right knee, raised his joined palms toward the Buddha, and said:

segs.p: “desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṁ, desetu sugato dhammaṁ.
segs.e: “Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Holy One teach the Dhamma!

segs.p: Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti.
segs.e: There are beings with little dust in their eyes. They’re in decline because they haven’t heard the teaching.
There will be those who understand the teaching!”

segs.p: Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṁ vatvā athāparaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: That is what the divinity Sahampati said. Then he went on to say:
“Among the Magadhans there appeared in the past
an impure teaching thought up by the stained.
Fling open the door to freedom from death!
Let them hear the teaching <j>the immaculate one discovered.
Standing high on a rocky mountain,
you can see the people all around.
In just the same way, All-seer, so intelligent,
having ascended the Temple of Truth,
rid of sorrow, look upon the people
swamped with sorrow,  <j>overcome by rebirth and old age.
Rise, hero! Victor in battle, caravan leader,
wander the world free of debt.
Let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma!
There will be those who understand!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā brahmuno ca ajjhesanaṁ viditvā sattesu ca kāruññataṁ paṭicca buddhacakkhunā lokaṁ volokesi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha, understanding the Divinity’s invitation, surveyed the world with the eye of a Buddha, out of his compassion for sentient beings.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā buddhacakkhunā lokaṁ volokento satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye, appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante.
segs.e: And the Buddha saw sentient beings with little dust in their eyes, and some with much dust in their eyes; with keen faculties and with weak faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and hard to teach. And some of them lived seeing the danger in the fault to do with the next world, while others did not.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṁ vā paduminiyaṁ vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṁ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṁvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni anto nimuggaposīni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṁvaḍḍhāni samodakaṁ ṭhitāni, appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṁvaḍḍhāni udakā accuggamma ṭhitāni anupalittāni udakena;
segs.e: It’s like a pool with blue water lilies, or pink or white lotuses. Some of them sprout and grow in the water without rising above it, thriving underwater. Some of them sprout and grow in the water reaching the water’s surface. And some of them sprout and grow in the water but rise up above the water and stand with no water clinging to them.

segs.p: evameva bhagavā buddhacakkhunā lokaṁ volokento addasa satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye, appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante.
segs.e: In the same way, the Buddha saw sentient beings with little dust in their eyes, and some with much dust in their eyes; with keen faculties and with weak faculties, with good qualities and with bad qualities, easy to teach and hard to teach. And some of them lived seeing the danger in the fault to do with the next world, while others did not.
When he had seen this he replied in verse to the divinity Sahampati:
“Flung open are the doors to freedom from death!
Let those with ears to hear commit to faith.
Thinking it would be troublesome, Divinity, <j>I did not teach
the sophisticated, sublime Dhamma among mankind.”

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati “katāvakāso khomhi bhagavatā dhammadesanāyā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then the divinity Sahampati, knowing that his request for the Buddha to teach the Dhamma had been granted, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.
Linked Discourses 6.2
1. The Appeal
Respect
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
segs.e: At one time, when he was first awakened, the Buddha was staying in Uruvelā at the root of the goatherd’s banyan tree on the bank of the Nerañjarā River.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: Then as he was in private retreat this thought came to his mind,

segs.p: “dukkhaṁ kho agāravo viharati appatisso, kaṁ nu khvāhaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyan”ti?
segs.e: “One without respect and reverence lives in suffering. What ascetic or brahmin should I honor and respect and rely on?”
Then it occurred to him:

segs.p: “aparipuṇṇassa kho sīlakkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: “I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of ethics, if it were incomplete.

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya attanā sīlasampannataraṁ aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā, yamahaṁ sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who is more accomplished than myself in ethics, who I should honor and respect and rely on.

segs.p: Aparipuṇṇassa kho samādhikkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of immersion, if it were incomplete.

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ passāmi sadevake loke …pe… attanā samādhisampannataraṁ aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā, yamahaṁ sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin … who is more accomplished than myself in immersion …

segs.p: Aparipuṇṇassa paññākkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of wisdom, if it were incomplete.

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ passāmi sadevake …pe… attanā paññāsampannataraṁ aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā, yamahaṁ sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin … who is more accomplished than myself in wisdom …

segs.p: Aparipuṇṇassa kho vimuttikkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of freedom, if it were incomplete.

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ passāmi sadevake …pe… attanā vimuttisampannataraṁ aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā, yamahaṁ sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin … who is more accomplished than myself in freedom …

segs.p: Aparipuṇṇassa kho vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhassa pāripūriyā aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: I’d honor and respect and rely on another ascetic or brahmin so as to complete the entire spectrum of the knowledge and vision of freedom, if it were incomplete.

segs.p: Na kho panāhaṁ passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya attanā vimuttiñāṇadassanasampannataraṁ aññaṁ samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā, yamahaṁ sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyaṁ.
segs.e: But I don’t see any other ascetic or brahmin in this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans—who is more accomplished than myself in the knowledge and vision of freedom, who I should honor and respect and rely on.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ yvāyaṁ dhammo mayā abhisambuddho tameva dhammaṁ sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I honor and respect and rely on the same Dhamma to which I was awakened?”

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the divinity Sahampati knew the Buddha’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in front of the Buddha.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: He arranged his robe over one shoulder, raised his cupped palms toward the Buddha, and said:
“That’s so true, Blessed One! That’s so true, Holy One!

segs.p: Yepi te, bhante, ahesuṁ atītamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tepi bhagavanto dhammaññeva sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya vihariṁsu;
segs.e: All the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas who lived in the past honored and respected and relied on this same teaching.

segs.p: yepi te, bhante, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā tepi bhagavanto dhammaññeva sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharissanti.
segs.e: All the perfected ones, the fully awakened Buddhas who will live in the future will honor and respect and rely on this same teaching.

segs.p: Bhagavāpi, bhante, etarahi arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammaññeva sakkatvā garuṁ katvā upanissāya viharatū”ti.
segs.e: May the Blessed One, who is the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha at present, also honor and respect and rely on this same teaching.”

segs.p: Idamavoca brahmā sahampati, idaṁ vatvā athāparaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: That is what the divinity Sahampati said. Then he went on to say:
“All Buddhas in the past,
the Buddhas of the future,
and the Buddha at present—
destroyer of the sorrows of many—
respecting the true teaching
they did live, they do live,
and they also will live.
This is the nature of the Buddhas.
Therefore someone who desires self-knowledge,
and aspires to greatness themselves,
should respect the true teaching,
remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”
Linked Discourses 6.3
1. The Appeal
With Brahmadeva
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā brāhmaṇiyā brahmadevo nāma putto bhagavato santike agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain brahmin lady had a son named Brahmadeva, who had gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in the presence of the Buddha.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā brahmadevo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Brahmadeva, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā brahmadevo arahataṁ ahosi.
segs.e: And Venerable Brahmadeva became one of the perfected.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā brahmadevo pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then Brahmadeva robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Sāvatthī for alms.

segs.p: Sāvatthiyaṁ sapadānaṁ piṇḍāya caramāno yena sakamātu nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Wandering indiscriminately for almsfood in Sāvatthī, he approached his own mother’s home.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmato brahmadevassa mātā brāhmaṇī brahmuno āhutiṁ niccaṁ paggaṇhāti.
segs.e: Now at that time Brahmadeva’s mother, the brahmin lady, was presenting a regular oblation to the Divinity.
Then the divinity Sahampati thought,

segs.p: “ayaṁ kho āyasmato brahmadevassa mātā brāhmaṇī brahmuno āhutiṁ niccaṁ paggaṇhāti.
segs.e: “This Venerable Brahmadeva’s mother, the brahmin lady, offers up a regular oblation to the Divinity.
Why don’t I go and stir up a sense of urgency in her?”

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—brahmaloke antarahito āyasmato brahmadevassa mātu nivesane pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in the home of Brahmadeva’s mother.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati vehāsaṁ ṭhito āyasmato brahmadevassa mātaraṁ brāhmaṇiṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then the divinity Sahampati, while standing in the air, addressed Brahmadeva’s mother in verse:
“Far from here is the realm of divinity, madam,
to which you present a regular oblation.
But the Divinity doesn’t eat that kind of food.
Why pray, <j>when you don’t know the path to divinity?
This Brahmadeva, madam,
free of attachments, has surpassed the gods.
Owning nothing, providing for no other, <j>a mendicant

segs.p: Yo te so piṇḍāya gharaṁ paviṭṭho.
segs.e: has entered your house for alms.
He’s worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, <j>a knowledge master, evolved.
He’s worthy of a religious donation <j>from gods and men.
Having banished all evils, he’s unsullied.
Cool at heart, he wanders searching for food.
He has no before and after,
peaceful, unclouded, untroubled, <j>with no need for hope,
he has laid down the rod <j>for all creatures firm and frail.
So let him enjoy your offering of alms for the highest.
With peaceful mind, he has left the crowd,
he wanders like a tamed elephant, unperturbed.
He’s a mendicant fair in ethics, with heart well freed.
So let him enjoy your offering <j>of alms for the highest.
With unwavering confidence in him,
present your religious donation <j>to one who is worthy of it.
Now that you’ve seen the sage who has crossed over, <j>madam,
make merit for the sake of future happiness!”
With unwavering confidence in him,
she presented her religious donation <j>to one who is worthy of it.
After seeing the sage who had crossed over, <j>the brahmin lady
made merit for the sake of future happiness.
Linked Discourses 6.4
1. The Appeal
With Baka the Divinity
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bakassa brahmuno evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ hoti:
segs.e: Now at that time Baka the Divinity had the following harmful misconception:

segs.p: “idaṁ niccaṁ, idaṁ dhuvaṁ, idaṁ sassataṁ, idaṁ kevalaṁ, idaṁ acavanadhammaṁ, idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati, ito ca panaññaṁ uttari nissaraṇaṁ natthī”ti.
segs.e: “This is permanent, this is everlasting, this is eternal, this is whole, this is not liable to pass away. For this is where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn. And there’s no other escape beyond this.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā bakassa brahmuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—jetavane antarahito tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha knew Baka the Divinity’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in that realm of divinity.

segs.p: Addasā kho bako brahmā bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: Baka the Divinity saw the Buddha coming off in the distance
and said to him,
“Come, good fellow! Welcome, good fellow!

segs.p: Cirassaṁ kho, mārisa, imaṁ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṁ idhāgamanāya.
segs.e: It’s been a long time since you took the opportunity to come here.

segs.p: Idañhi, mārisa, niccaṁ, idaṁ dhuvaṁ, idaṁ sassataṁ, idaṁ kevalaṁ, idaṁ acavanadhammaṁ, idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati. Ito ca panaññaṁ uttari nissaraṇaṁ natthī”ti.
segs.e: For this is permanent, this is everlasting, this is eternal, this is whole, this is not liable to pass away. For this is where there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn. And there’s no other escape beyond this.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā bakaṁ brahmānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “avijjāgato vata bho bako brahmā, avijjāgato vata bho bako brahmā.
segs.e: “Alas, Baka the Divinity is lost in ignorance! Alas, Baka the Divinity is lost in ignorance!

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma aniccaṁyeva samānaṁ niccanti vakkhati, adhuvaṁyeva samānaṁ dhuvanti vakkhati, asassataṁyeva samānaṁ sassatanti vakkhati, akevalaṁyeva samānaṁ kevalanti vakkhati, cavanadhammaṁyeva samānaṁ acavanadhammanti vakkhati.
segs.e: Because what is actually impermanent, not lasting, transient, incomplete, and liable to pass away, he says is permanent, everlasting, eternal, whole, and not liable to pass away.

segs.p: Yattha ca pana jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca cavati ca upapajjati ca, tañca tathā vakkhati:
segs.e: And where there is being born, growing old, dying, passing away, and being reborn, he says that

segs.p: ‘idañhi na jāyati na jīyati na mīyati na cavati na upapajjati’.
segs.e: there’s no being born, growing old, dying, passing away, or being reborn.

segs.p: Santañca panaññaṁ uttari nissaraṇaṁ, ‘natthaññaṁ uttari nissaraṇan’ti vakkhatī”ti.
segs.e: And although there is another escape beyond this, he says that there’s no other escape beyond this.”
“Gotama, we seventy-two merit-makers <j>are now wielders of power,
having passed beyond rebirth and old age.
This is our last rebirth as the Divinity, <j>O knowledge master.
And now many people pray to us.”
“But, Baka, the lifespan here is short, not long,
though you think it’s long.
A hundred thousand times a hundred million years—
I understand your lifespan, Divinity.”
“I am the blessed one of infinite vision,
who has gone beyond rebirth and old age and sorrow.
What was my past practice of precept and observance?
Explain to me so that I may understand.”
“You gave drink to many humans
who were oppressed by thirst and heat.
That’s your past practice of precept and observance.
I recollect it like one who has wakened from sleep.
When people at Deer River Bank were seized,
you released the captives as they were led away.
That’s your past practice of precept and observance.
I recollect it like one who has wakened from sleep.
When a boat on the Ganges River was seized
by a fierce dragon desiring human flesh,
you freed it wielding mighty force.
That’s your past practice of precept and observance.
I recollect it like one who has wakened from sleep.
I used to be your footman named Kappa.
You thought he was intelligent and loyal.
That’s your past practice <j>of precept and observance.
I recollect it like one who has wakened from sleep.”
“You certainly understand this lifespan of mine.
And others, too, you know; <j>that’s why you’re the Buddha.
And that’s why your blazing glory
lights up even the realm of divinity.”
Linked Discourses 6.5
1. The Appeal
A Certain Divinity
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarassa brahmuno evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ hoti:
segs.e: Now at that time a certain divinity had the following harmful misconception:

segs.p: “natthi so samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo idha āgaccheyyā”ti.
segs.e: “No ascetic or brahmin can come here!”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa brahmuno cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso …pe… tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha knew that divinity’s train of thought. As easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in that realm of divinity.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṁ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā.
segs.e: Then the Buddha sat cross-legged in the air above that divinity, having entered upon the fire element.
Then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna thought,
“Where is the Buddha staying at present?”

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavantaṁ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṁ pallaṅkena nisinnaṁ tejodhātuṁ samāpannaṁ.
segs.e: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, he saw the Buddha seated cross-legged in the air above that divinity, having entered upon the fire element.

segs.p: Disvāna—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—jetavane antarahito tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahosi.
segs.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, he vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in that realm of divinity.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno puratthimaṁ disaṁ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṁ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṁ bhagavato.
segs.e: Then Mahāmoggallāna—positioning himself in the east, below the Buddha—sat cross-legged in the air above that divinity, having entered upon the fire element.
Then Venerable Mahākassapa …

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhagavantaṁ dibbena cakkhunā …pe…
disvāna—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso …pe… evameva—jetavane antarahito tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahosi.
Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo dakkhiṇaṁ disaṁ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṁ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṁ bhagavato.
segs.e: positioned himself in the south …
Venerable Mahākappina …

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā mahākappino bhagavantaṁ dibbena cakkhunā …pe… tejodhātuṁ samāpannaṁ.
Atha kho āyasmā mahākappino pacchimaṁ disaṁ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṁ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṁ bhagavato.
segs.e: positioned himself in the west …
Venerable Anuruddha …

segs.p: Addasā kho āyasmā anuruddho …pe… tejodhātuṁ samāpannaṁ.
Disvāna—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso …pe… tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahosi.
Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho uttaraṁ disaṁ nissāya tassa brahmuno upari vehāsaṁ pallaṅkena nisīdi tejodhātuṁ samāpajjitvā nīcataraṁ bhagavato.
segs.e: positioned himself in the north, below the Buddha, sitting cross-legged in the air above that divinity, having entered upon the fire element.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ brahmānaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Mahāmoggallāna addressed that divinity in verse:
“Reverend, do you still have the same view
that you had in the past?
Or do you see the radiance
surpassing the realm of divinity?”
“Good fellow, I don’t have that view
that I had in the past.
I see the radiance
surpassing the realm of divinity.
So how could I say today
that I am permanent and eternal?”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā taṁ brahmānaṁ saṁvejetvā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—tasmiṁ brahmaloke antarahito jetavane pāturahosi.
segs.e: Having inspired a sense of awe in the Divinity, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, the Buddha vanished from the realm of divinity and reappeared in Jeta’s Grove.

segs.p: Atha kho so brahmā aññataraṁ brahmapārisajjaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then that divinity addressed a member of his retinue,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, mārisa, yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ evaṁ vadehi:
segs.e: “Please, good fellow, go up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and say to him:

segs.p: ‘atthi nu kho, mārisa moggallāna, aññepi tassa bhagavato sāvakā evaṁmahiddhikā evaṁmahānubhāvā;
segs.e: ‘Moggallāna my good fellow, are there any other disciples of the Buddha who have power and might

segs.p: seyyathāpi bhavaṁ moggallāno kassapo kappino anuruddho’”ti?
segs.e: comparable to the worthies Moggallāna, Kassapa, Kappina, and Anuruddha?’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, mārisā”ti kho so brahmapārisajjo tassa brahmuno paṭissutvā yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, good fellow,” replied that retinue member. He went to Moggallāna and asked as instructed.

segs.p: “atthi nu kho, mārisa moggallāna, aññepi tassa bhagavato sāvakā evaṁmahiddhikā evaṁmahānubhāvā;
seyyathāpi bhavaṁ moggallāno kassapo kappino anuruddho”ti?
Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno taṁ brahmapārisajjaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then Mahāmoggallāna addressed that member of the retinue of Divinity in verse:
“There are many disciples of the Buddha
who have the three knowledges,
and have attained psychic power, <j>expert in encompassing minds,
they’re perfected ones with defilements ended.”

segs.p: Atha kho so brahmapārisajjo āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā yena so brahmā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ brahmānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then that member of the retinue of Divinity, having approved and agreed with what Mahāmoggallāna said, went to that divinity and said to him,
“Good fellow, Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:
segs.s: that member of the retinue of Divinity

segs.e: ‘There are many disciples of the Buddha
segs.s: that member of the retinue of Divinity

segs.e: who have the three knowledges,
segs.s: that member of the retinue of Divinity

segs.e: and have attained psychic power, <j>expert in encompassing minds,
segs.s: that member of the retinue of Divinity

segs.e: they’re perfected ones with defilements ended.’”
segs.s: that member of the retinue of Divinity

segs.e: That is what that member of the retinue of Divinity said.

segs.p: Attamano ca so brahmā tassa brahmapārisajjassa bhāsitaṁ abhinandīti.
segs.e: Satisfied, that divinity approved what the member of his retinue said.
Linked Discourses 6.6
1. The Appeal
The Negligent Divinity
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṁ dvārabāhaṁ upanissāya aṭṭhaṁsu. Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā suddhāvāsaṁ paccekabrahmānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa went to the Buddha and stationed themselves one by each door-post. But Subrahmā said to Suddhāvāsa,
“Good fellow, it’s the wrong time to pay homage to the Buddha.
He has gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Asuko ca brahmaloko iddho ceva phīto ca, brahmā ca tatra pamādavihāraṁ viharati.
segs.e: But such-and-such realm of divinity is successful and prosperous, while the divinity living there is negligent.

segs.p: Āyāma, mārisa, yena so brahmaloko tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ brahmānaṁ saṁvejeyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Come, let’s go to that realm of divinity and inspire awe in that divinity!”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, mārisā”ti kho suddhāvāso paccekabrahmā subrahmuno paccekabrahmuno paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, good fellow,” replied Suddhāvāsa.

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso …pe… evameva—bhagavato purato antarahitā tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahesuṁ.
segs.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, they vanished from in front of the Buddha and appeared in that realm of divinity.

segs.p: Addasā kho so brahmā te brahmāno dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna te brahmāno etadavoca:
segs.e: That divinity saw those divinities coming off in the distance and said to them,
“Well now, good fellows, where have you come from?”

segs.p: “Āgatā kho mayaṁ, mārisa, amha tassa bhagavato santikā arahato sammāsambuddhassa.
segs.e: “Good fellow, we’ve come from the presence of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Gaccheyyāsi pana tvaṁ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti?
segs.e: Shouldn’t you go to attend on that Blessed One?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutto, kho so brahmā taṁ vacanaṁ anadhivāsento sahassakkhattuṁ attānaṁ abhinimminitvā subrahmānaṁ paccekabrahmānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When they had spoken, that divinity refused to accept their advice. He multiplied himself a thousand times and said to Subrahmā,

segs.p: “passasi me no tvaṁ, mārisa, evarūpaṁ iddhānubhāvan”ti?
segs.e: “Good fellow, can’t you see that I have such psychic power?”
segs.s: that divinity refused to accept their advice

segs.e: “I see that, good fellow.”

segs.p: “So khvāhaṁ, mārisa, evaṁmahiddhiko evaṁmahānubhāvo kassa aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā upaṭṭhānaṁ gamissāmī”ti?
segs.e: “Since I have such psychic power and might, what other ascetic or brahmin should I go to and attend upon?”
segs.s: that divinity refused to accept their advice

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā dvisahassakkhattuṁ attānaṁ abhinimminitvā taṁ brahmānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Subrahmā multiplied himself two thousand times and said to that divinity,

segs.p: “passasi me no tvaṁ, mārisa, evarūpaṁ iddhānubhāvan”ti?
segs.e: “Good fellow, can’t you see that I have such psychic power?”
“I see that, good fellow.”

segs.p: “Tayā ca kho, mārisa, mayā ca sveva bhagavā mahiddhikataro ceva mahānubhāvataro ca.
segs.e: “That Buddha has even more psychic power and might than you or me.

segs.p: Gaccheyyāsi tvaṁ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti?
segs.e: Shouldn’t you go to attend on that Blessed One?”

segs.p: Atha kho so brahmā subrahmānaṁ paccekabrahmānaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
segs.e: Then that divinity addressed Subrahmā in verse:
“There are three hundreds of phoenixes, <j>four of swans,
and five of tigerhawks. <j>To he who practiced absorption
belongs this palace; it shines, Divinity,
lighting up the northern quarter!”
“So what if your palace shines,
lighting up the northern quarter?
A clever person, seeing the strife in form,
its chronic trembling, takes no pleasure in it.”

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā taṁ brahmānaṁ saṁvejetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṁsu.
segs.e: Then after inspiring awe in that divinity, the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa vanished right there.

segs.p: Agamāsi ca kho so brahmā aparena samayena bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassāti.
segs.e: And after some time that divinity went to attend on the Buddha.
Linked Discourses 6.7
1. The Appeal
About Kokālika
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṁ dvārabāhaṁ nissāya aṭṭhaṁsu.
segs.e: Then the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa went to the Buddha and stationed themselves one by each door-post.

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then Subrahmā spoke this verse about the mendicant Kokālika in the Buddha’s presence:
“What wise person here would judge
the immeasurable by measuring them?
I think anyone who’d do such a thing
is an ordinary person, shrouded.”
Linked Discourses 6.8
1. The Appeal
About Katamorakatissaka
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

segs.p: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṁ dvārabāhaṁ nissāya aṭṭhaṁsu.
segs.e: Then the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa went to the Buddha and stationed themselves one by each door-post.

segs.p: Atha kho suddhāvāso paccekabrahmā katamodakatissakaṁ bhikkhuṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: Then Suddhāvāsa spoke this verse about the mendicant Katamorakatissaka in the Buddha’s presence:
“What wise person here would judge
the immeasurable by measuring them?
I think anyone who’d do such a thing
is an ignoramus, shrouded.”
Linked Discourses 6.9
1. The Appeal
With the Divinity Tudu
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena kokāliko bhikkhu ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time the mendicant Kokālika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho turū paccekabrahmā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena kokāliko bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāsaṁ ṭhito kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious independent divinity Tudu, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the mendicant Kokālika, and standing in the air he said to him,
“Kokālika, have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna,
they’re good monks.”
“Who are you, reverend?”
“I am Tudu the independent divinity.”

segs.p: “Nanu tvaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā anāgāmī byākato, atha kiñcarahi idhāgato?
segs.e: “Didn’t the Buddha declare you a non-returner? So what then are you doing back here?
See how far you have strayed!”
“A person is born
with an axe in their mouth.
A fool cuts themselves with it
when they say bad words.
When you praise someone worthy of criticism,
or criticize someone worthy of praise,
you choose a losing hand with your own mouth:
you’ll never find happiness that way.
A losing hand at dice is a trivial thing,
if all you lose is your money
and all you own, even yourself.
What’s a really terrible hand
is to hate the holy ones.
For a hundred thousand times a hundred million,
times five hundred and thirty-six times <j>a thousand times ten million years
a slanderer of noble ones goes to hell,
having aimed bad words and thoughts at them.”
Linked Discourses 6.10
1. The Appeal
With Kokālika
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the mendicant Kokālika went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “pāpicchā, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā pāpikānaṁ icchānaṁ vasaṁ gatā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When this was said, the Buddha said to Kokālika,

segs.p: “mā hevaṁ, kokālika, avaca; mā hevaṁ, kokālika, avaca.
segs.e: “Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!

segs.p: Pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.
segs.e: Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna, they’re good monks.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time Kokālika said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kiñcāpi me, bhante, bhagavā saddhāyiko paccayiko; atha kho pāpicchāva bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā pāpikānaṁ icchānaṁ vasaṁ gatā”ti.
segs.e: “Despite my faith and trust in the Buddha, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, the Buddha said to Kokālika,

segs.p: “mā hevaṁ, kokālika, avaca; mā hevaṁ, kokālika, avaca.
segs.e: “Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!

segs.p: Pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.
segs.e: Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna, they’re good monks.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time Kokālika said to the Buddha,
“Despite my faith and trust in the Buddha, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have corrupt wishes. They’ve fallen under the sway of corrupt wishes.”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho bhagavā kokālikaṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, the Buddha said to Kokālika,
“Don’t say that, Kokālika! Don’t say that, Kokālika!
Have confidence in Sāriputta and Moggallāna, they’re good monks.”

segs.p: Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Kokālika rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Acirapakkantassa ca kokālikassa bhikkhuno sāsapamattīhi pīḷakāhi sabbo kāyo phuṭo ahosi.
segs.e: Not long after he left his body erupted with boils the size of mustard seeds.

segs.p: Sāsapamattiyo hutvā muggamattiyo ahesuṁ, muggamattiyo hutvā kalāyamattiyo ahesuṁ, kalāyamattiyo hutvā kolaṭṭhimattiyo ahesuṁ, kolaṭṭhimattiyo hutvā kolamattiyo ahesuṁ, kolamattiyo hutvā āmalakamattiyo ahesuṁ, āmalakamattiyo hutvā beluvasalāṭukamattiyo ahesuṁ, beluvasalāṭukamattiyo hutvā billamattiyo ahesuṁ, billamattiyo hutvā pabhijjiṁsu. Pubbañca lohitañca pagghariṁsu.
segs.e: The boils grew to the size of mung beans, then chickpeas, then jujube seeds, then jujubes, then myrobalans, then unripe wood-apples, then ripe wood-apples. Finally they burst open, and pus and blood oozed out.

segs.p: Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu teneva ābādhena kālamakāsi.
segs.e: Then the mendicant Kokālika died of that illness.

segs.p: Kālaṅkato ca kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṁ nirayaṁ upapajji sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā.
segs.e: He was reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to him,
“Sir, the mendicant Kokālika has passed away.

segs.p: Kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṁ nirayaṁ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā”ti.
segs.e: He was reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”
That is what the divinity Sahampati said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then he bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened.

segs.p: “imaṁ, bhikkhave, rattiṁ brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati maṁ etadavoca:
Kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṁ nirayaṁ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā’ti.
Idamavoca, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati, idaṁ vatvā maṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kīvadīghaṁ nu kho, bhante, padume niraye āyuppamāṇan”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how long is the lifespan in the Pink Lotus hell?”
“It’s long, mendicant.
It’s not easy to calculate

segs.p: ‘ettakāni vassāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasatāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasahassāni iti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassāni iti vā’”ti.
segs.e: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it lasts.”
“But sir, is it possible to give a simile?”
“It’s possible,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho. Tato puriso vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena ekamekaṁ tilaṁ uddhareyya;
segs.e: “Suppose there was a Kosalan load of twenty packs of sesame seed. And at the end of every hundred years someone would remove a single seed from it.

segs.p: khippataraṁ kho so, bhikkhu, vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho iminā upakkamena parikkhayaṁ pariyādānaṁ gaccheyya, na tveva eko abbudo nirayo.
segs.e: By this means the Kosalan load of twenty packs of sesame seed would run out faster than a single lifetime in the Abbuda hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati abbudā nirayā, evameko nirabbudanirayo.
segs.e: Now, twenty lifetimes in the Abbuda hell equal one lifetime in the Nirabbuda hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati nirabbudā nirayā, evameko ababo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Nirabbuda hell equal one lifetime in the Ababa hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ababā nirayā, evameko aṭaṭo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Ababa hell equal one lifetime in the Aṭaṭa hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati aṭaṭā nirayā, evameko ahaho nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Aṭaṭa hell equal one lifetime in the Ahaha hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ahahā nirayā, evameko kumudo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Ahaha hell equal one lifetime in the Yellow Lotus hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati kumudā nirayā, evameko sogandhiko nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Yellow Lotus hell equal one lifetime in the Fragrant Water Lily hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati sogandhikā nirayā, evameko uppalanirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Fragrant Water Lily hell equal one lifetime in the Blue Water Lily hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati uppalā nirayā, evameko puṇḍariko nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the Blue Water Lily hell equal one lifetime in the White Lotus hell.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati puṇḍarikā nirayā, evameko padumo nirayo.
segs.e: Twenty lifetimes in the White Lotus hell equal one lifetime in the Pink Lotus hell.

segs.p: Padume pana, bhikkhu, niraye kokāliko bhikkhu upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṁ āghātetvā”ti.
segs.e: The mendicant Kokālika has been reborn in the Pink Lotus hell because of his resentment for Sāriputta and Moggallāna.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“A person is born
with an axe in their mouth.
A fool cuts themselves with it
when they say bad words.
When you praise someone worthy of criticism,
or criticize someone worthy of praise,
you choose a losing hand with your own mouth:
you’ll never find happiness that way.
A losing hand at dice is a trivial thing,
if all you lose is your money
and all you own, even yourself.
What’s a really terrible hand
is to hate the holy ones.
For a hundred thousand times a hundred million,
times five hundred and thirty-six times <j>a thousand times ten million years
a slanderer of noble ones goes to hell,
having aimed bad words and thoughts at them.”

segs.p: Bako ca brahmā aparā ca diṭṭhi;
Turū ca brahmā aparo ca kokālikoti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 6.11
Chapter Two
With Sanaṅkumāra
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati sappinītīre.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the bank of the Serpentine River.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sanaṅkumāro abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ sappinītīraṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sanaṅkumāra, lighting up the entire Serpentine riverbank, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“The aristocrat is best among people
who take clan as the standard.
But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct
is best among gods and humans.”
That is what the divinity Sanaṅkumāra said,
and the Teacher concurred.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sanaṅkumāro “samanuñño me satthā”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.
segs.e: Then the divinity Sanaṅkumāra, knowing that the Teacher concurred, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before vanishing right there.
Linked Discourses 6.12
Chapter Two
About Devadatta
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate acirapakkante devadatte.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain, not long after Devadatta had left.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ gijjhakūṭaṁ pabbataṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entire Vulture’s Peak, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati devadattaṁ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: and spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:
“The banana plant is destroyed by its own fruit,
as are the bamboo and the reed.
Honor destroys a reprobate,
as pregnancy destroys a mule.”
Linked Discourses 6.13
Chapter Two
At Andhakavinda

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā māgadhesu viharati andhakavinde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Magadhans at Andhakavinda.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ abbhokāse nisinno hoti, devo ca ekamekaṁ phusāyati.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha was meditating in the open during the dark of night, while a gentle rain drizzled down.

segs.p: Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ andhakavindaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious divinity Sahampati, lighting up the entirety of Andhakavinda, went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato santike imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: and recited these verses in the Buddha’s presence:
“One should frequent secluded lodgings,
and practice to be released from fetters.
If you don’t find enjoyment there,
live in the Saṅgha, self-protected and mindful.
Walking for alms from family to family,
with senses guarded, alert and mindful.
One should frequent secluded lodgings,
free of fear, freed in the fearless.
Where dreadful reptiles slither,
where the lightning flashes and the heavens thunder
in the dark of the night;
there meditates a mendicant, free of goosebumps.
For this is ever seen by me,
it isn’t just the testament of hearsay.
Within a single spiritual dispensation
there are a thousand conquerors of Death.
And of trainees, more than five hundred,
and ten times ten tens,
are all stream-enterers,
freed from rebirth in the animal realm.
And as for the rest of folk
who I think have shared in merit—
I couldn’t even number them,
for fear of speaking falsely.”
Linked Discourses 6.14
Chapter Two
About Aruṇavatī
So I have heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī.
There he addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Once upon a time, mendicants, there was a king named Aruṇavā.

segs.p: Rañño kho pana, bhikkhave, aruṇavato aruṇavatī nāma rājadhānī ahosi.
segs.e: He had a capital named Aruṇavatī.

segs.p: Aruṇavatiṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, rājadhāniṁ sikhī bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho upanissāya vihāsi.
segs.e: Sikhī the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha lived supported by Aruṇavatī.

segs.p: Sikhissa kho pana, bhikkhave, bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa abhibhūsambhavaṁ nāma sāvakayugaṁ ahosi aggaṁ bhaddayugaṁ.
segs.e: Sikhī had a fine pair of chief disciples named Abhibhū and Sambhava.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho abhibhuṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicant Abhibhū,

segs.p: ‘āyāma, brāhmaṇa, yena aññataro brahmaloko tenupasaṅkamissāma, yāva bhattassa kālo bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Come, brahmin, let’s go to one of the realms of divinity until it’s time for our meal.’

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ, bhante’ti kho bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paccassosi.
segs.e: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho abhibhū ca bhikkhu—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—aruṇavatiyā rājadhāniyā antarahitā tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahesuṁ.
segs.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, they vanished from Aruṇavatī and appeared in that realm of divinity.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho abhibhuṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicant Abhibhū,

segs.p: ‘paṭibhātu, brāhmaṇa, taṁ brahmuno ca brahmaparisāya ca brahmapārisajjānañca dhammī kathā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Brahmin, teach the Dhamma as you feel inspired for that divinity, his assembly, and the members of his retinue.’

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā, brahmānañca brahmaparisañca brahmapārisajje ca dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṁsesi.
segs.e: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū. Then he educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired them with a Dhamma talk.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti:
segs.e: But the Divinity, his assembly, and his retinue complained, grumbled, and objected,

segs.p: ‘acchariyaṁ vata, bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, kathañhi nāma satthari sammukhībhūte sāvako dhammaṁ desessatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! How on earth can a disciple teach Dhamma in the presence of the Teacher?’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho abhibhuṁ bhikkhuṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicant Abhibhū,

segs.p: ‘ujjhāyanti kho te, brāhmaṇa, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca—
segs.e: ‘Brahmin, the Divinity, his assembly, and his retinue are complaining

segs.p: acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, kathañhi nāma satthari sammukhībhūte sāvako dhammaṁ desessatīti.
segs.e: that a disciple teaches Dhamma in the presence of the Teacher.

segs.p: Tena hi tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, bhiyyoso mattāya brahmānañca brahmaparisañca brahmapārisajje ca saṁvejehī’ti.
segs.e: Well then, brahmin, stir them up even more!’

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā dissamānenapi kāyena dhammaṁ desesi, adissamānenapi kāyena dhammaṁ desesi, dissamānenapi heṭṭhimena upaḍḍhakāyena adissamānena uparimena upaḍḍhakāyena dhammaṁ desesi, dissamānenapi uparimena upaḍḍhakāyena adissamānena heṭṭhimena upaḍḍhakāyena dhammaṁ desesi.
segs.e: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū. Then he taught Dhamma with his body visible; with his body invisible; with the lower half visible and the upper half invisible; and with the upper half visible and the lower half invisible.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmā ca brahmaparisā ca brahmapārisajjā ca acchariyabbhutacittajātā ahesuṁ:
segs.e: And the Divinity, his assembly, and his retinue, their minds full of wonder and amazement, thought,

segs.p: ‘acchariyaṁ vata bho, abbhutaṁ vata bho, samaṇassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing! The ascetic has such psychic power and might!’

segs.p: Atha kho abhibhū bhikkhu sikhiṁ bhagavantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Abhibhū said to the Buddha Sikhī,

segs.p: ‘abhijānāmi khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhikkhusaṅghassa majjhe evarūpiṁ vācaṁ bhāsitā—
segs.e: ‘Sir, I recall having said this in the middle of the Saṅgha:

segs.p: pahomi khvāhaṁ, āvuso, brahmaloke ṭhito sahassilokadhātuṁ sarena viññāpetun’ti.
segs.e: “Standing in the realm of divinity, I can make my voice heard throughout the thousandfold galaxy.”’
‘Now is the time, brahmin! Now is the time, brahmin!

segs.p: yaṁ tvaṁ, brāhmaṇa, brahmaloke ṭhito sahassilokadhātuṁ sarena viññāpeyyāsī’ti.
segs.e: Standing in the realm of divinity, make your voice heard throughout the thousandfold galaxy.’

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, abhibhū bhikkhu sikhissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā brahmaloke ṭhito imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: ‘Yes, sir,’ replied Abhibhū. Standing in the realm of divinity, he spoke this verse:
‘Rouse yourselves! Try harder!
Devote yourselves to the teachings of the Buddha!
Crush the army of Death,
as an elephant a hut of reeds.
Whoever shall meditate diligently
in this teaching and training,
giving up transmigration through rebirths,
will make an end of suffering.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī ca bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho abhibhū ca bhikkhu brahmānañca brahmaparisañca brahmapārisajje ca saṁvejetvā—
segs.e: Having inspired that divinity, his assembly, and his retinue with a sense of awe,

segs.p: seyyathāpi nāma …pe… tasmiṁ brahmaloke antarahitā aruṇavatiyā rājadhāniyā pāturahesuṁ.
segs.e: as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, Sikhī and Abhibhū vanished from that realm of divinity and appeared in Aruṇavatī.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sikhī bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha Sikhī addressed the mendicants,

segs.p: ‘assuttha no tumhe, bhikkhave, abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti?
segs.e: ‘Mendicants, did you hear the mendicant Abhibhū speaking a verse while standing in a realm of divinity?’

segs.p: ‘Assumha kho mayaṁ, bhante, abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We did, sir.’

segs.p: ‘Yathā kathaṁ pana tumhe, bhikkhave, assuttha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti?
segs.e: ‘But what exactly did you hear?’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho mayaṁ, bhante, assumha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassa:
segs.e: ‘This is what we heard, sir:
“Rouse yourselves! Try harder!
Devote yourselves to the teachings of the Buddha!
Crush the army of Death,
as an elephant a hut of reeds.
Whoever shall meditate diligently
in this teaching and training,
giving up transmigration through rebirths,
will make an end of suffering.”

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ kho mayaṁ, bhante, assumha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’ti.
segs.e: That’s what we heard, sir.’
‘Good, good, mendicants!

segs.p: sādhu kho tumhe, bhikkhave, assuttha abhibhussa bhikkhuno brahmaloke ṭhitassa gāthāyo bhāsamānassā’”ti.
segs.e: It’s good that you heard the mendicant Abhibhū speaking this verse while standing in a realm of divinity.’”

segs.p: Idamavoca bhagavā, attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: That is what the Buddha said. Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.
Linked Discourses 6.15
Chapter Two
Full Extinguishment

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kusinārāyaṁ viharati upavattane mallānaṁ sālavane antarena yamakasālānaṁ parinibbānasamaye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying between a pair of sal trees in the sal forest of the Mallas at Upavattana near Kusinārā at the time of his full extinguishment.
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:
“Come now, mendicants, I say to you all:
‘Conditions fall apart. Persist with diligence.’”
These were the Realized One’s last words.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Paṭhamā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Ākāsānañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Viññāṇañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Ākiñcaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpajji.
segs.e: Then the Buddha entered the first absorption. Emerging from that, he entered the second absorption. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the third absorption, the fourth absorption, the dimension of infinite space, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of nothingness, and the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. Then he entered the cessation of perception and feeling.

segs.p: Saññāvedayitanirodhā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Ākiñcaññāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Viññāṇañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samāpajji. Ākāsānañcāyatanā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Paṭhamā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Dutiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Tatiyā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpajji. Catutthā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantaraṁ bhagavā parinibbāyi.
segs.e: Then he emerged from the cessation of perception and feeling and entered the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the dimension of nothingness, the dimension of infinite consciousness, the dimension of infinite space, the fourth absorption, the third absorption, the second absorption, and the first absorption. Emerging from that, he successively entered into and emerged from the second absorption and the third absorption. Then he entered the fourth absorption. Emerging from that the Buddha immediately became fully extinguished.

segs.p: Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā brahmā sahampati imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: When the Buddha was fully quenched, along with the full extinguishment, the divinity Sahampati spoke this verse:
“All creatures in this world
must lay down this bag of bones.
For even a Teacher such as this,
unrivaled in the world,
the Realized One, attained to power,
the Buddha was fully quenched.”

segs.p: Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā sakko devānamindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Sakka, lord of gods, spoke this verse:
“Oh! Conditions are impermanent,
their nature is to rise and fall;
having arisen, they cease;
their settling is such bliss.”

segs.p: Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā ānando imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
segs.e: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Venerable Ānanda spoke this verse:
“Then there was terror!
Then they had goosebumps!
When the Buddha, endowed with all fine qualities,
was fully quenched.”

segs.p: Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā anuruddho imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
segs.e: When the Buddha was fully quenched, Venerable Anuruddha spoke this verse:
“There was no more breathing
for the unaffected one of steady heart.
Imperturbable, committed to peace,
the Clear-eyed One was fully quenched.
He put up with painful feelings
without flinching.
The liberation of his heart
was like the extinguishing of a lamp.”
The Linked Discourses on the Divinity are complete.
